label: Rejected Ban Zhao's Confucian "Three Obediences" in favor of women's emancipation
description: Qiu Jin explicitly attacked traditional Confucian didactic manuals tracing back to Ban Zhao's Lessons for Women, condemning ritual female subordination and footbinding as instruments of patriarchal bondage.
dialecticalTension: Breaks sharply from classical Confucian harmony to demand revolutionary civic equality.

citations.author: Lydia H. Liu, Rebecca E. Karl & Dorothy Ko
citations.work: The Birth of Chinese Feminism: Essential Texts in Transnational Theory

label: Catalyzed radical late-Qing feminist print discourse preceding Natural Justice
description: Qiu Jin's founding of the Chinese Women's Journal and revolutionary martyrdom in 1907 electrified Chinese feminist circles in Tokyo, where He-Yin Zhen launched Tianyi bao (Natural Justice) the same year.
dialecticalTension: Prepares the radical transition from nationalist feminist reform to structural anarcho-feminism.
historicalContext: 1904–1907 Sino-Japanese radical intellectual networks in Tokyo and Shanghai.
